title: Separating ATE and First-Best Welfare Estimation Rates under Critically Vanishing Overlap
banked_reason: D0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < field gate 7.4; welfare rate remains bracketed between n^-2/5(log n)^2/5 and n^-2/5 log n in a narrow known-design benchmark.
gap_reasons: The welfare rate is not characterized sharply: the note proves a lower bound of n^{-2/5}(log n)^{2/5} and an upper bound of n^{-2/5}log n, so the delivered contribution is a strict precision separation rather than a welfare minimax frontier.

The separation is established only in a deliberately narrow benchmark with a fixed x^{5/2}/2 propensity, known control response, anchored one-dimensional C^2 effects, and known design quantities, which limits its immediate econometric scope.
paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived and the D0.5 math and decision referees passed the strict welfare-versus-ATE precision separation, including the known-zero-ATE subclass and an attested Cai–Low moment-dual citation. The general referee capped the contribution at subfield because its welfare minimax logarithmic exponent remains bracketed between 2/5 and 1 and the experiment is narrow. A future field-tier run would need a sharper welfare frontier or a substantively broader model with new proofs.
tldr: In a known binary causal experiment with an explicit full-data lift and treatment probability \(e(x)=x^{5/2}/2\), the observed law identifies both the ATE and unrestricted first-best value. The proved ATE minimax absolute-risk and \(95\%\)-honest connected-interval length are both of order \(n^{-2/5}\). In contrast, even on \(\mathcal F_0\), where the ATE is exactly zero and known, the proved welfare lower bounds are \(n^{-2/5}(\log n)^{2/5}\), while the explicit observable estimator and finite-sample honest interval achieve \(n^{-2/5}\log(e+n)\). Thus optimal-value precision is separated from ATE precision by a diverging logarithmic factor; the exact welfare logarithmic exponent remains open.
gap: Optimal-value inference currently relies on regular zero-set geometry or strong positivity, while weak-overlap minimax theory primarily treats linear functionals. No located result compares ATE and unrestricted optimal-value precision within the same critical boundary experiment, especially when the ATE is known.
fill: The project proves matched ATE risk and honest-length rates, lower bounds welfare risk and honest length by a larger logarithmic order on the known-zero-ATE subclass, and supplies an observable welfare estimator and finite-sample interval, leaving only the exact logarithmic exponent open.
